name: Jabez
charge: Calling on the God of Israel to bless him indeed, enlarge his coast, keep His hand with him, and keep him from evil
summary: Among the families of Judah the record stops on one man. Jabez was more honourable than his brethren, and his mother called his name Jabez because she bore him with sorrow. He called on the God of Israel and asked that He would bless him indeed, enlarge his coast, keep His hand with him, and keep him from evil, that it might not grieve him. And God granted him what he requested.
offenseFull: The chapter gathers more of the families of Judah, the sons that came from him and the line of Hur the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem, and keeps the households in order down to the sons of Coz (1 Chronicles 4:1-8). The names in that stretch carry meaning, which is why the scribe keeps them. In the middle of the list the record stops on one man: Jabez was more honourable than his brethren, and his mother called his name Jabez because she bore him with sorrow (1 Chronicles 4:9), the meaning of the name matching the scripture itself.

Jabez called on the God of Israel and asked that He would bless him indeed, enlarge his coast, keep His hand with him, and keep him from evil, so that it might not grieve him (1 Chronicles 4:10). He did not call on the gods of the land around him; he called on the God of Israel, and he asked for four things: the blessing itself, land, the hand of the Lord with him, and to be kept from evil. It is the same ground Achsah stood on when she asked her father for the springs as well as the south land (Joshua 15:18-19), and the same calling on the name of the Lord that men began in the days of Enos (Genesis 4:26).
judgmentFull: And God granted him that which he requested (1 Chronicles 4:10). The Most High gave him what he asked for, and the record says no more about him. It gives no offense, no judgment and no chronology; it gives a man of Judah, born in sorrow, who called on the God of Israel and was heard, and it sets him in the middle of a genealogy rather than in a history of his deeds.

The teaching of the chapter around him is that the blessing rested heavily on Judah. When the same chapter turns to the sons of Simeon it notes that Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brethren had not many children, and Simeon did not multiply like the children of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:24-27). The blessing of increase was on Judah, and Jabez stands inside it as a single name the scribe would not pass over. Simeon was not left without mercy either: the princes of Simeon, whose houses increased, went to seek pasture for their flocks and found fat and quiet pasture in a land where the sons of Ham had dwelt of old, and smote those habitations in the days of Hezekiah; and five hundred of them went to mount Seir, smote the remnant of the Amalekites that had escaped, and dwelt there (1 Chronicles 4:38-43).

text.text: The sons of Judah; Pharez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal.
And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai, and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
And these were of the father of Etam; Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi:
And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Beth–lehem.
And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
And the sons of Helah were, Zereth, and Jezoar, and Ethnan.
And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
And Jabez was more honourable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him with sorrow.

And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.
And it came to pass, as she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou?
Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.
And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.
The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul:
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
And the sons of Mishma; Hamuel his son, Zacchur his son, Shimei his son.
And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah.
These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly.
And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old.

And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents, and the habitations that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day.
